stops.name: Parco naturale del Mont Avic
stops.detail: The natural park of Mont Avic (in French, Parc naturel du Mont Avic) is a protected natural area of the Aosta Valley and has an area of over 5,747 hectares. The first regional natural park of the region, after the Gran Paradiso National Park, created in 1989 and expanded in [dated source], is extended between the Champdepraz valley and the Champorcher Valley, crossed by the Chalamy stream, in a secluded position compared to the great Valdostane tourist routes. The high peaks of the Avic mountains (3,003 m), Iverta (2.936 m) and Glacier (3.186 m) separate the Champdepraz valley from the Champorcher valley. In the park there is the largest pine forest (Pinus mugo subsp. the Aosta Valley: over 980 hectares.
